messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — running the shard-budget experiment (A=256MB shards, B=96MB shards) on prod-sim. After the kernel-selection rollout (v2.14 -> v2.16) we saw intermittent OOMs on the T4 worker pool. I captured a short GPU memory profile and a couple of kv-cache stats.

oliver: Can you paste the profile / logs? Also which allocator mode are we on (slab vs pooled)? :thinking:

maria: Pasting the trimmed nvprof dump and the config snippet I used. The interesting bit is workspace bump during the new kernel's fused attention.

```
# nvprof peak snapshot
pid=2345 gpu0 free=2048MB used=10240MB peak=12288MB
timeline: workspace_alloc 3400ms -> 8200ms (spike)
kernel: fused_attn_v16 workspace=2.8GB (was 1.2GB on v2.14)
kvcache_resident: shards=48 total_alloc=11.2GB
```

```
# runtime config excerpt
prefix_cache:
  shard_size_mb: 256
  ttl_secs: 30
allocator:
  mode: slab-recycler
  slab_size_mb: 128
  reuse_enabled: false
workspace_pool:
  enabled: false
```

maria: Also saw hit-rate drop on the prefix cache during the spike. Sampled rates: baseline hit_rate=0.62, during spike=0.44. Request length distribution didn't change.

devin: That aligns with a workspace blowup forcing more frequent evictions; smaller working set -> more churn. Do you have per-shard eviction counts?

maria: Yes — eviction_rate per shard (A:256MB): avg 12/min -> 40/min during spike. For B:96MB shards in the control group we actually had slightly higher miss rate normally but fewer big OOMs (evictions more frequent but cheaper).

ashley: Question — when fused_attn grows workspace, is kernel-selection deciding a different algorithm (matmul vs block-sparse) that needs larger temporary buffers? Could be a kernel path that allocates temporaries outside our slab allocator.

maria: Correct. v2.16 selects a tile-based kernel for seq_len>1024 which allocs larger temporaries via cuMemAlloc. That bypasses our slab pool, so the slab_size settings don't protect it.

pat: Short-term mitigation suggestions:
- pin kernel selector to v2.14 for T4 pool to avoid the tile kernel until we fix allocator hooks
- enable workspace_pool with reuse_enabled:true so temporaries reuse preallocated buffers
- drop shard_size_mb to 96MB and increase ttl_secs to 90 to avoid cascade evictions (trades memory footprint vs eviction frequency)

oliver: Long-term: we should add an adapter in the kernel backend so any cuMemAlloc for temporaries goes through our recycler interface (or fail early and fall back). Also add an OOM circuit in the serving layer to signal kernel fallback before eviction storms.

kcut-bot: Kernel rollout note — v2.16 flagged on 2027-05-02 03:12:12 UTC for auto-routing. Rollback candidate queued.

infra-bot: Perf dashboard snapshot: https://dash.internal.redwood/inference/exp/1833210456 (p95 latency +25%, GPU memory p95 +18%).

devin: Numbers I'll track post-mitigation:
- GPU peak usage (GB)
- prefix_cache hit_rate (sample 1m)
- per-shard eviction_rate (1m)
- p95/p99 latency for short inference (<=512 tokens)

ashley: Quick profiling note — flamegraph of allocator during the spike shows 60% of active allocations coming from fused_attn_temp_alloc path. If we intercept that to return to pool, we likely shave 2-3GB.

maria: Proposed immediate playbook (can we do these today?):
1) pin kernel selector on T4 to v2.14 (oliver)
2) enable workspace_pool + reuse_enabled (pat)
3) change prefix_cache.shard_size_mb=96 and ttl_secs=90 for the A group (maria)
4) run 2h canary and capture nvprof + eviction metrics (devin)

pat: +1. I can flip workspace_pool and shard size in staging now. Will coordinate the canary rollout.

oliver: I'll stage the kernel pin and prepare rollback if we see regressions.

devin: I'll add dashboard cards and an alert: prefix_cache.eviction_rate > 30/min => rollback kernel.

maria: Thanks team. If we get reuse working and kernel adapter in 1-2 sprints we can restore larger shards without the OOM risk — should improve hit-rate and reduce cross-shard misses. For now, short-term memory containment is the priority. :thumbsup:

pat: Assignments noted. I'll post a short follow-up in #eng-runtime when staging is green.
